text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL

- Consortia led by AirTouch Communications Inc of the United States and France Telecom are winners in tender for two lucrative GSM licences in Romania, the paper quoted a Communications Ministry source a saying. The ministry told Reuters it cannot confirm the report.
- Furniture factories affected by shortage of timber.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Lead smelter at Baia Mare is main source of pollution for the city, investigations by the Committee for environmental protection showed.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Number of companies listed on OTC market remains small.
- Industry Ministry to cut subsidies and jobs in mining sector.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Romania's economy needs startegic investors, says in interview Emil Dima, State Ownerhsip Fund president.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA:
- Centrist Democratic Convention (CDR) bloc and Social Democratic Union (USD) signed accord to support CDR's candidate in presidential run-offs and to form coalition government.

- The Central Electoral Bureau (BEC) released final results in November 3 parliamentary polls, which put CDR in a leading position in both chambers, followed by the former ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) and USD.
- Some 2,000 votes for the CDR were deleted from the computer in the Transylvanian county of Bihor.
- President Ion Iliescu is expected to put a distance between himself and the PDSR in the campaign for the November 17 run-offs, due to the party's dropping popularity.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- President Ion Iliescu declined invitation by his competitor Emil Constantinescu to hold electoral debate in the Western city of Timisoara.
- BEC will set quota of votes to be redistributed to the six parties and alliances which passed the 3.0 percent threshold for parliament.
- Zaher Iskandarani, accused of 41 billion lei in tax evasion, has been released from prison pending trial.
ADEVARUL
- CDR and USD jointly obtained more than 53 percent of votes in both parliament chamber.
- Campaigning President Iliescu pledged to "defend the masses from the right wing's offensive".
- Newspaper lists seats obtained after parliament polls on Sunday by the six parties which entered the legislative body.
- Six-member family dies from cooking gas poisoning in the eastern town of Fetesti.
- Priest Simeon Tatu, a PDSR senator, accused the opposition National Peasant Party -- backbone of the CDR -- of trying to split the Romanian Orthodox Church, newspaper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Some 70 cases of hepatitis were registered in Bucharest schools and kindergartens.
- Iliescu slams his competitor, Emil Constantinescu, for "unrealistic, populist and demagogical promisses" to voters.
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- Romania's liberal parties PNL, PNL-CD and ANL could form a coalition before the November 17 presidential run-offs.
- Petre Roman expects living standards to rise in two years, when the new government brings in real reform measures.
LIBERTATEA
- Some 300,000 children to get free vaccines for hepatitis.

- Local administration autonomy, fiscal reform with serious cuts of profit and salary tax, a rise in child allowances higher pensions and unemployment benefits top list of priorities for the future CDR-USD government.
ZIUA

- If elected after run-off, President Ion Iliescu can cause a government crisis by refusing to appoint a prime minister from the CDR-USD coalition which won parliament elections. The constitution says parliament approves a prime minister named by the president or has to dissolve itself. ($= 3,449 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
